one_line: A synchronized watch-along that lets GPT observe and discuss the same video moment as the viewer.
what_it_does: Loads YouTube, direct video, or embeddable media and exposes time-aligned observations, captions, reactions, and context through the existing agent conversation.
leverage_rationale: Shared timing, rolling captions, and media state make the agent materially more reliable than UI-driving a player, while the conversation remains the memory surface.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly centers sharing the same live video moment.
ABOUT describes cadence-based WebMCP observations and caption capture.
Frames show watch-together UI, search/selection, embedded video, and webcam presence.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent central workflow from selecting media to watching with an agent, with video evidence of multiple states; end-to-end agent invocation is not directly shown.
execution_evidence: 173-second submission video with three frame sheets.
Frames show input, suggestions, loaded video, captions and persistent participant tile.
Devpost packaging and pitch agree on the product concept.
impact_rationale: Viewers who want explanation or companionship during video have a clear, credible use case, especially for dense or educational media.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies timing and interruption as the problem versus post-hoc summarization.
Supports speech-heavy video and captions.
Frames show a usable watch-along experience.
creativity_rationale: It is a fresh interaction model: the agent is present at the media moment rather than a detached summarizer or sidebar chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly rejects a second chatbot and post-video summarizer.
Combines synchronized media observation with an existing conversation.
Video demonstrates the distinctive watch-together framing.
usability_note: Clear watch/search flow and quiet-by-default cadence; dense media context may still require tuning.
red_flags: Agent tool calls and actual reactions are not plainly legible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Good alignment between pitch, frames, and interaction model.
advance_reason: Distinctive agent-in-the-moment experience with strong evidence of a coherent product.

one_line: An identity, audit, and reputation layer that lets sites distinguish trusted agents from anonymous automation.

leverage_rationale: The product is itself structured agent access and shared trust state; ordinary UI automation cannot provide equivalent identity, attribution, and reputation semantics reliably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT defines AuditEvent records with identity, tool, result, reputation delta, and resulting score.

Reputation affects agent-specific limits.

standouts: Excellent consent boundary and evidence-linked review flow.

advance_reason: One of the clearest packets: high WebMCP leverage, coherent safety model, and visible product workflow.
